items.title: International Biotechnology Trust: Sanofi deal highlights accelerating biotech M&A wave
items.summary: International Biotechnology Trust Plc (LSE:IBT, OTC:IBITF) portfolio manager Ailsa Craig talked with Proactive's Stephen Gunnion about Sanofi’s US$41 billion acquisition of Insmed, the implications for shareholders and the growing wave of mergers and acquisitions across biotechnology. Craig explained how the trust’s actively managed strategy targets companies with characteristics attractive to major pharmaceutical groups. Insmed was its largest portfolio holding ahead of the deal, with Sanofi’s US$175-per-share offer representing a 46% premium to the pre-announcement share price and potentially boosting the trust’s net asset value (NAV). She also discussed the sustainability of the trust’s dividend, explaining how acquisition proceeds support its capital-funded dividend policy. Craig said the M&A wave was gathering pace, with ten portfolio companies involved in deals this year, against nine last year and a historical annual average of four to five. She identified the pharmaceutical industry's approaching patent cliff, with around US$400 billion in drug sales facing patent expirations, as a major catalyst. More than 70% of new drugs last year originated in biotechnology, underlining the sector’s growing importance to pharmaceutical innovation.
